name: MSU Green
lede: MSU Green is a very dark, slightly blue green used as a school color, its initials standing for a state university rather than any pigment or dye.

sections.title: An institution's green
sections.body:
Our library traces the name only to a Wikipedia color list, which does not say which of several schools using the initials MSU it names, or when the color was adopted [1]. The near-duplicate name Zydeco appears in the same library entry at a distance of only 1.5, suggesting two independent namings landed on almost the same dark green [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[brunswick-green]], 3.3 units of CIEDE2000 away and described as almost the same [1]. [[amulet]] sits a little farther out at 3.6, lighter, and [[dark-hunter-green]] at 3.9, greener [1]. Measured in LCH, it sits at lightness 26, among the darkest greens in our library [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 119 of 23,781 paintings (0.5 percent), more common than 55 percent of the named colors, as photographed [2]. Paul Gauguin is its most devoted painter, using it in 5 of the 50 Gauguin works in our archive, a rate 6.8 times the baseline of the museums those works come from [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 19 of 1,674 paintings, at 3.5 times the expected rate [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays a shadow, 47 percent of the time, or a hidden color, 45 percent, a role measured by lightness rank within the canvas [2]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so a color match is not a pigment test [2].
